traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report covers multiple protocol variants (Pour plate - Manual 1 plate & 2 plates, Pour plate - Automated, Spreading 1 plate & 2 plates) for each of 7 food categories, shown in Figure 3 (accuracy profile study, pp.36-41) and Appendix 7/8 raw data. I recorded the primary variant (Pour plate - Manual - 1 plate interpretation) bias/SD/lower-upper β-ETI values per category as the canonical relative trueness table, since these correspond most directly to the required category/type mapping. The other variants (Pour plate Manual 2 plates, Pour plate Automated, Spreading 1&2 plates) give very similar bias/SD values (all well within the ±0.5 log Acceptability Limit) and are described in the report's Figure 3 tables but not extracted individually here. Note the document also contains a broader 'method comparison study / relative trueness study' section (3.1, pages 8-34, with raw data in Appendix 4) organized by product type (meat products, etc.) rather than by the 7 numbered ISO categories used in the accuracy profile study (section 3.2); the per-category accuracy-profile table (Figure 3) was used here as it directly ties bias/SD/CI to the 7 canonical food categories with an explicit Acceptability Limit of ±0.5 log10. The inter-laboratory study (section 4, Tables 16-17) reports pooled Low/Medium/High level statistics rather than per-food-category data, so it was not used for the category table but is consistent with the ±0.5 log AL. Certificate number taken from cover page: 'BRD 07/24 – 11/13'.
